literal: To meet together so as to delight, and to part so as to be thought of with longing, such is the characteristic nature of the learned.
translation: To meet with delight and to part with a lingering longing to meet again—such is the way of the learned.
modern: மகிழ்ச்சியடையும்படி கூடிப் பேசி, பிரியும்போது மீண்டும் நினைத்துப் பார்க்கும் படியாகப் பிரிவதே கற்றறிந்தவர்களின் இயல்பாகும்.
explanation: This couplet beautifully defines the nature of intellectual companionship. When scholars meet, their interaction is filled with mutual joy and intellectual stimulation, represented by the word 'uvappa' (to delight). When they part, they do not simply forget each other; instead, they leave a lasting impression that makes them think of and long for each other's company, represented by 'uḷḷa' (to think of with longing). The poet suggests that the ultimate test of a meaningful, learned relationship is that it brings joy in presence and a sweet, reflective longing in absence.
